summary: A one-screen variable-font concept site: the katakana word 'カチカチ' fills a black screen and the pointer position drives two custom axes (KIKI↔BOUBA stroke shape on x, CONTRAST on y), with the live percentages printed at the four screen edges. There is no scrolling content; an ABOUT page and a light/dark invert button sit in a thin top bar.

instances.look: Thin top bar (never cut as its own block, attached to screen 00): underlined 'KACHI-BUWA' + '• A Katakana Variable Font Concept' at the left, 'ABOUT' and a small white circle button at the right, a white hairline rule below
instances.ux: Name links home, ABOUT opens a separate page, the circle button toggles the page between black-on-white and white-on-black (html.invert)
instances.learn: A single round button as the whole theme switch keeps the chrome down to one line

reconstruction.layout: Full-width bar ~40px tall, 12px side padding, 1px white rule at the bottom; circle button ~16px at the far right
reconstruction.typography: ~12px MS Gothic (monospaced Japanese system font, served as a webfont), mixed case, name underlined
reconstruction.behaviour: button.btn-invert toggles the 'invert' class on <html>, swapping background and text colours
reconstruction.html: div.info > div#in > p (name link + tagline), div#toplink a[href=about.html], button.btn.btn-invert

instances.look: The whole site and its hero: 'カチカチ' (kachi-kachi, 'click-clack') in white, ~250px tall, centred on black, with four small edge labels: 'NO CONTRAST 50%' top centre, 'CONTRAST 50%' bottom centre, 'KIKI 0%' left middle, 'BOUBA 0%' right middle. Screen 01 shows a second state (KIKI/BOUBA 50%) where the strokes turn sharp and the horizontal strokes thin into long hairlines that run past the letters
instances.feel: Experimental, tactile, witty (the kiki/bouba sound-shape effect as a font axis)
instances.ux: No handles to grab: moving the pointer left↔right blends the stroke ends from spiky 'kiki' to round 'bouba' (axis KIKI), up↔down blends from no contrast to high contrast (axis CONT); the edge labels count the percentages live. The heading carries data-reset and a 'contenteditable' class, so the word can apparently be retyped and reset. The capture is a wheel capture: the second screen is the same component in another axis state
instances.learn: Name the four edges of the screen after the extremes of two axes and print their live percentages there: the viewport itself becomes the 2D slider and its legend

reconstruction.layout: Single 100vh black screen, no scroll; word centred horizontally and vertically, ~1080px wide (x≈190–1270) and ~250px tall; edge labels absolutely positioned: top centre (y≈52px), bottom centre (y≈886px), left middle (x≈14px), right middle (right≈14px); empty #left and #right divs split the screen in halves
reconstruction.typography: Word: Kachi6GX variable (custom axes KIKI 0–100 and CONT 0–100) at ~280px, white; labels ~12px MS Gothic uppercase, tracked slightly, white
reconstruction.behaviour: mousemove → x maps to KIKI 0–100% (BOUBA label shows the complement), y maps to CONT 0–100% (top label NO CONTRAST, bottom CONTRAST); font-variation-settings updated on h1#hl and the label spans #backcount, #slantcount, #contrast_onecount, #contrast_twocount updated; white flash for ~0.5s on load before the invert class applies
reconstruction.content: One onomatopoeic katakana word, カチカチ, the same sound game as the kiki/bouba experiment
reconstruction.assets: Custom variable katakana font (Kachi6GX.ttf); MS Gothic for UI
reconstruction.html: div.contrast_one/#contrast_onecount, div.contrast_two/#contrast_twocount, div.backslant/#backcount (KIKI), div.slant/#slantcount (BOUBA); section.cover h1#hl.mainheading.contenteditable[data-reset=カチカチ]; credits in an HTML comment: inspired by Times New Arial (Liebermann Kiepe Reddemann, Elias Hanzer) and Jonas Pelzer
